newsitem.title: GERMANY: No decision on Frankfurt airport/station land use.
newsitem.headline: No decision on Frankfurt airport/station land use.

text.p: Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG), the owner and manager of Frankfurt Airport, said it was still considering different options for the future use of ground above a new underground train station.
FAG and German Railways (DB) were jointly reviewing several proposals for the high-speed Inter City Express (ICE) station but no decision has yet been made, an FAG statement said.
It followed a German newspaper report that a leisure park with theatres and cinemas seating several thousand people but with no car parking could be built.
The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reported that DB favoured the maximum possible leisure use of the land while FAG wanted a mix of a new hotel, offices and leisure facilities.
Johannes Ender, FAG commercial director, said in the statement that such speculation was "too early" but the decision would take economic and corporate considerations into account.

The station on the new Frankfurt-Cologne high-speed rail line is due to open in 1999 and feature passenger and baggage check-in facilities. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
